content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.7) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or dips below 0.3 — model ignores downside risk and fails to adjust downward.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then overcorrects in the opposite direction.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often misses early downward trends, especially when sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model overweights momentum and fails to account for potential reversal.
- Model underestimates sharp downward moves after recent highs — especially when sentiment drops below 0.3 or shows negative momentum.
- Forecasting should adjust downward if sentiment history shows recent negative sentiment (e.g., last 3–5 days < 0.3) — model tends to ignore this.
- Avoid overconfidence in upward momentum — if sentiment is high but recent price action shows signs of exhaustion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days of lower highs), reduce forecast slope.
